title: CNAS Launches AI Policy Lab
gist: CNAS launched an AI Policy Lab led by Paul Scharre, adding five experts on AI compute, economic competition and frontier security, with core areas of AI security/safety, AI economic competition, compute governance, and military AI adoption. Promotional release with hiring list.

insights.claim: CNAS launched the AI Policy Lab, led by Executive Vice President Paul Scharre, adding five research experts focused on AI compute, economic competition, and frontier security issues.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Think-tank capacity on compute governance is scaling, foreshadowing more detailed chip/compute policy proposals in Washington.
insights.locator: CNAS will inaugurate the new lab

insights.claim: The lab's core research areas are AI security and safety, AI economic security and competition, compute governance, and military AI adoption and assurance.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Compute governance and military AI are the policy fronts most likely to affect chip exporters and defense-tech vendors.

insights.claim: Vivek Chilukuri will direct AI technology policy research, Emily Kilcrease AI economic security and competition, and Stacie Pettyjohn military AI research within the lab.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Names to watch for policy signals on export controls and defense AI.
insights.locator: Scharre will be joined in leading

insights.claim: CNAS says its experts and alumni have written the rules for how the Pentagon incorporates autonomous systems and served at the highest levels of AI policymaking.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: CNAS output is a credible lead indicator for Pentagon AI/autonomy policy direction.
insights.quote: CNAS experts and alumni have written the rules for how the Pentagon incorporates autonomous systems
insights.locator: By bridging the divide between innovators

insights.claim: CNAS CEO Richard Fontaine argued that Washington must adapt to the lightning speed of AI development, with the lab aiming to make policy match the pace of innovation.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Expect faster-moving AI regulation and security policy proposals.
insights.quote: Washington must adapt to the lightning speed of AI development

insights.claim: The lab is hiring leads for compute governance and for AI and competition policy, plus AI safety and security researchers and an AI engineer, indicating compute and competition policy are priority build-out areas.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Compute governance is becoming an institutionalized policy discipline — relevant to datacenter and chip-export regulation.
insights.locator: To support the expansion of CNAS’s AI
